skill.name: gmgn-token-buy
skill.description: Turn a token name into a vetted, sized buy order. Two things here are exclusive to this skill: resolving a NAME or symbol to the one right contract among its copycats, and sizing an order — amount, slippage, gas, position. No sibling does either. USE THIS SKILL WHEN a buy is being prepared, which shows up as a NAME or symbol, or an AMOUNT, or both — including the plainest possible ask with no mention of checking: 我想买 200u 的 PENGU, 帮我买 500 刀的 BONK, 买 1 个 SOL 的 WIF, 帮我买点 dogwifhat, 想梭 100u 的 XX, PENGU 现在能买吗, PENGU 能不能买, 能不能冲, 值不值得进, 确认是正主不是仿盘再买, buy me $500 of PENGU — and including a bare contract address once an amount arrives with it. DO NOT USE THIS SKILL for a bare contract address with no name to resolve and no amount to size (「这个地址能不能买」, 打个分, 尽调, 有没有貔貅, rug check, is this token safe): that one belongs to gmgn-contract-dd, which is the skill that returns the 0-100 safety verdict. This skill never computes a second verdict of its own — it CALLS gmgn-contract-dd and defers to it — so there is nothing to gain by taking that ask, and the user gets an order card they never asked for. Come back here the moment they name an amount. A buy question about a LAUNCHER rather than about a token — 「这个 dev 的新盘能不能买」, 「他下一个盘值不值得冲」, "should I buy his next launch", "will this dev rug at open" — is gmgn-dev-score: it scores the creator's own record, and there is no token name to resolve or amount to size yet. Come back here once they name the coin. Naming a token with no buy intent at all is gmgn-market search. gmgn-swap is where this skill ENDS, not a rival for it: gmgn-swap signs and submits, and this skill never touches a private key and never places an order, so a plain buy request starts HERE and reaches gmgn-swap only after the user confirms the order card. Note that gmgn-swap cannot start from a name either — its --output-token is a contract address and the only names it resolves are the currencies SOL/BNB/ETH/USDC — so 帮我买点 dogwifhat has to come here regardless of who is asked. Go straight to gmgn-swap only when the user says the pre-buy check is unwanted (skip the checks, 直接买, 不用尽调, 我很急), or for what this skill does not do at all: selling, percentage sells, limit orders, stop loss, take profit, trailing orders, multi-wallet batch trading, order status, gas-price lookups. The split is by what the ask still needs done, not by who executes: a name needs resolving and an amount needs sizing, so both start here; a bare address needs only a verdict, so it is gmgn-contract-dd's; a signed transaction is always gmgn-swap's.
skill.summary: Resolve a token name, screen the contract, size the purchase, and prepare a confirmation-ready GMGN order card.
skill.author: gmgnai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans and Chinese text triggering entropy heuristics. Six external-command findings and the IPv6 endpoint request are confirmed. Semantic review also found unsafe API-key handling and delegation to a transaction-signing skill.

remediation.issue: The setup asks users to send an API key through chat and passes it as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to configure credentials locally through a masked prompt or standard input, and never display secret-bearing output.

remediation.issue: User-supplied token names and addresses are inserted into shell command examples without quoting or explicit validation.
remediation.suggestion: Pass arguments without a shell, validate chain and address formats, and quote user-controlled search terms when a shell is unavoidable.

remediation.issue: IPv6 troubleshooting contacts a third-party endpoint and reveals the user's public IPv6 address.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for consent before the request, document the disclosure, or replace it with a local connectivity check.

remediation.issue: The workflow delegates an irreversible token purchase to a skill that holds trading credentials and a private key.
remediation.suggestion: Require the executor to present the final chain, contract, amount, fees, and slippage before obtaining a separate confirmation.

content.user_title: Prepare a Vetted GMGN Token Buy
content.value_statement: Buying by token name can select a copycat or create unsafe order parameters. This skill resolves the contract, screens risks, and prepares a confirmed order card.
actual_capabilities: Resolves a token name, symbol, or supplied address to a specific contract.
Supports Solana, Ethereum, BSC, Base, Robinhood, Arc, and Stable chains.
Checks trading volume, liquidity depth, market direction, holder data, and contract safety.
Calculates slippage, price impact, gas options, and estimated token quantity.
Produces a structured order card and delegates execution only after explicit confirmation.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated gmgn-cli.
Supports only seven listed chains and stops when required safety data is unavailable.
Depends on GMGN response quality and may report missing or conflicting data.
Does not sign transactions, hold private keys, or execute purchases directly.

use_cases.title: Check a Named Token
use_cases.description: Resolve a token symbol among copycats and review the selected contract before preparing a purchase.

use_cases.title: Size a New Position
use_cases.description: Estimate slippage, price impact, gas, and received quantity for a specified purchase amount.

use_cases.title: Standardize Buy Reviews
use_cases.description: Apply consistent liquidity, volume, direction, and safety gates before handing an order to execution.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve and Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [TOKEN] is suitable to buy and identify the correct contract.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review using a token name or symbol

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Fixed Buy
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a vetted [AMOUNT] buy of [TOKEN] on [CHAIN]. Stop if any required check fails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Order preparation with a known budget

prompt_templates.title: Compare Same-Name Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve [TOKEN] across supported chains, explain the leading contract, and ask me to choose when evidence is inconclusive.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Conservative Order Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [TOKEN] for a [AMOUNT] purchase using strict gates, calculated slippage, protected execution, and complete fee disclosure.

output_examples.input: Prepare a 200 USDC purchase of PENGU.
output_examples.output: A buy order card identifies the full contract, reports four screening results, estimates slippage and fees, then requests confirmation.

output_examples.input: Can I buy WIF without specifying a chain?
output_examples.output: A candidate comparison lists matching contracts and evidence. The skill asks for chain selection when it cannot identify one contract reliably.

output_examples.input: Review this token when security data is unavailable.
output_examples.output: The report marks the safety gate as missing and does not prepare executable order parameters.

best_practices: Verify the full contract address before confirming any order.
Treat missing safety, liquidity, or fee data as unresolved risk.
Review amount, slippage, gas, price impact, and protected execution settings together.
anti_patterns: Do not select the first search result or trust a token name as proof of identity.
Do not bypass failed screening gates because other indicators appear favorable.
Do not share private keys or API keys in the conversation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute the purchase?
faq.answer: No. It prepares parameters and delegates execution to gmgn-swap only after explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Which chains are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Solana, Ethereum, BSC, Base, Robinhood, Arc, and Stable.

faq.question: Can it identify the correct contract from a symbol?
faq.answer: It compares matching contracts using relevance, liquidity, volume, market value, holders, and age. It asks when evidence remains inconclusive.

faq.question: What happens when a safety check fails?
faq.answer: The skill reports the failed gate and stops order preparation unless the user explicitly acknowledges an allowed exception.

faq.question: Does it need my private key?
faq.answer: No. This skill does not access private keys. Transaction signing belongs to gmgn-swap.

faq.question: How does it choose slippage and gas?
faq.answer: It derives slippage from taxes, price impact, and recent volatility. It presents available gas tiers and marks estimates clearly.
